executive_assessment.text: Historical drought and heat vary across Dobrudzha, the Danube corridor and Struma/Mesta valleys. Asparuhovo provides one dated example of unequal housing losses, not a national household risk ranking.

Recent government analysis identifies named-town network losses, peripheral-settlement service constraints and irrigation limitations. Climate pressure is one contributor alongside infrastructure and governance.
Commission findings identify risk-information, implementation and coordination gaps; program allocations and municipal commitments are capacities, not proven outcomes.

geographic_notes.text: Source dated 2024-12-31 reports: 1981–2010 drought mapping identifies the Danube corridor and central north to the Pre-Balkans; Northeast Bulgaria/Dobrudzha is most affected, with pockets around Blagoevgrad, Petrich–Sandanski and Mesta valley.

Source dated 2024-12-31 reports: Struma valley near Kresna Gorge is hottest: some years had 6–8 days above 40°C; 1961–2020 records show 40–55 hot days/year there versus 2–3 on the northern Black Sea coast.

Source dated 2021-03 reports: For the June 2014 torrential-rain flash flood in Asparuhovo (Varna), the WB box reports 122 evacuated families, Roma ownership of 60% of destroyed houses, and 14 deaths, most among Roma.

Source dated 2021-03 reports: The report links unequal flood losses in Asparuhovo to informal Roma housing that failed building-code/zoning standards and to inadequate municipal prevention; it says no clear data show how many Roma live in flood-prone areas.

The March 2026 MOEW summary reports high water-network loss indicators for Shumen, Pernik, Targovishte, Haskovo, Yambol and Pazardzhik. These service-system losses are not attributed to climate change; underlying operator periods vary.

Source dated 2026-06-03 reports: Only around 24% of Bulgaria's population lives in Covenant of Mayors coverage; 10 of 49 cities made adaptation commitments and 44% of signatories submitted SECAPs on time. Sofia has an adaptation strategy; Burgas a development vision.

known_gaps.text: Automated machine-screening is not independent source verification. Routine/default app-use approval does not certify claims or sources. 13 of 14 evidence records and 0 of 0 pathways lack claim-level verification in this remediation; review the linked records before relying on them.
No inspected public source established a climate-related armed/intercommunal violence pathway or an FCV-to-adaptation pathway; this is a search gap, not evidence of absence.
The 2024 NSI release gives population totals for municipalities partly or fully affected by disaster declarations, not direct counts of people harmed, and its text does not name those municipalities.
The Asparuhovo Roma evidence is a regional World Bank synthesis of cited sources; its casualty count was not independently reconciled with other event reports.

The Commission finds the national climate-risk assessment outdated and current comparable regional/local risk information insufficient; no inspected source supplied household-level vulnerability data for smaller settlements.
No verified source-stated climate-to-violence or conflict-to-adaptation chain was found. This is a search limitation, not proof of absence.

Asparuhovo findings describe differentiated Roma housing exposure and municipal prevention gaps in one 2014 case, not ethnic propensity to conflict. Reported casualties were not independently reconciled.

Municipality populations in disaster-declaration statistics are not counts of people directly harmed. Water-system loss indicators have varied reference periods and are not climate-attributable losses.
A health projection with no source-stated period was excluded rather than assigning a working horizon. Current comparable local vulnerability information remains incomplete.
Routine/default app-use approval granted by Lindsey Jones on 2026-10-27; independent source verification remains incomplete. Lending eligibility is not an FCV classification.
